title: UsageBar sanitized usage snapshot
description: Transport-neutral, privacy-minimized snapshot of current UsageBar quota state. Carries usage facts only: no credentials, no raw provider output, no filesystem paths, no device or account identity, no pre-rendered UI strings, and no transport configuration. Schema version 1 does not carry usage history.

schemaVersion.description: Wire contract version. Independent of the UsageBar product release version. An incompatible semantic change increments this.

generatedAt.description: When this snapshot document was built by the desktop sender. This is NOT a measurement time: a provider whose reading was retained from an earlier cycle keeps its own older measuredAt. Never derive per-provider freshness from this field.

providers.description: Providers the desktop is reporting on. An empty array means no provider is connected. A non-empty array in which no entry has collecting=true means every connected provider is paused.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 instant with an explicit offset, e.g. 2026-09-22T14:05:00Z. The pattern is a structural guard; consumers must additionally parse the value and reject unreasonable instants.

providerId.description: Stable machine identifier for a provider. Lowercase kebab slug, never a localized or display name. Known values in schema v1: 'codex', 'claude-code'. The open pattern lets a future provider appear without a schemaVersion bump; a consumer that does not recognise an id renders it generically rather than failing.

windowId.description: Canonical identity of one quota window within its provider, derived from the window's kind and qualifier: 'five-hour', 'weekly', 'weekly-<scope>', 'duration-<minutes>', 'unknown-<position>'. Unique within a provider. Used to reference the headline window.

kind.description: Structured category of this quota window, so the consumer can localize it without parsing windowId. 'duration' and 'unknown' are the forward-compatibility escape hatches: any future window with a known length is reported as 'duration', and any window whose length the desktop cannot determine is reported as 'unknown'. Neither requires a schemaVersion bump.

scope.description: Model or model-family qualifier for a weeklyScoped window, as a normalized lowercase slug ('opus', 'sonnet', 'premium-models'). Never raw provider text and never a translated label. This is what distinguishes Claude's ordinary all-models weekly window (kind 'weekly') from a model-specific weekly window (kind 'weeklyScoped', scope 'opus').

durationMinutes.description: Length of the quota window in minutes, when the desktop knows it. Required for kind 'duration'. Conventionally 300 for 'fiveHour' and 10080 for 'weekly'. Absent for 'unknown'.

position.description: Zero-based ordinal of an 'unknown' window as the provider reported it. This is the only identity an unknown window has.

remainingPercent.description: Quota remaining in this window, as a whole percent. This is the value UsageBar presents, already clamped and already past the desktop's display-noise filter. usedPercent is deliberately not transmitted: it is exactly 100 - remainingPercent and duplicating it would create a second source of truth.

resetsAt.description: When this window's quota resets, if the provider reported it. Absent means unknown, never 'no reset'.

measurement.description: The provider's retained last successful reading. Present only when the desktop actually holds one. A paused provider keeps its measurement, and keeps the measuredAt of when that reading was taken.

measuredAt.description: When this reading was actually taken and accepted by the desktop. This is the only correct basis for freshness. It does not advance when a later refresh cycle fails, nor when the provider is paused, nor when a new snapshot is generated.

headlineRemainingPercent.description: The single remaining-percent value UsageBar presents for this provider, already selected by the desktop's provider-specific headline policy. The consumer must not recompute it.

headlineWindowId.description: Which window in 'windows' produced headlineRemainingPercent. Must equal the windowId of exactly one entry in 'windows'. JSON Schema cannot express that cross-reference, so consumers must check it.

windows.description: Every quota window the provider currently reports. Window identities must be unique within this array; JSON Schema's uniqueItems cannot express uniqueness on one property, so consumers must check it.

connected.description: Whether the provider's configuration is retained on the desktop. Independent of 'collecting': pausing a provider leaves it connected, which is the entire point of a pause. These two facts are never conflated.

collecting.description: Whether the desktop is currently allowed to initiate readings for this provider. false with connected=true means the user paused it; the retained measurement stays and must not be discarded or treated as a failure.
